newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne says would talk with Invacare.
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne says would talk with Invacare.

text.p: Healthdyne Technologies Inc said it would open the door to Invacare Corp about a possible transaction if Invacare withdraws its tender offer.
In a letter to Invacare Chief Executive Malachi Mixon, Healthdyne Chairman Parker Petit said the company would hold talks with parties that have expressed an interest.

"We are willing to include Invacare in this process and furnish to Invacare the same non-public information concerning Healthdyne Technologies as we may furnish to such third parties, provided that Invacare agrees to abide by the same conditions being asked of such third parties," Petit wrote.
In addition to withdrawing the tender offer, Invacare would be required to stop soliciting proxies and sign a confidentiality agreement, Petit wrote.

"Of course, if Healthdyne Technologies' board determines to sell the company to the highest bidder, Invacare would be invited to make a proposal to the board, which the board would consider along with any other proposals we have received," Petit added.
Healthdyne said it would not provide Invacare with any information if it did not abide by those requirements.
Healthdyne has repeatedly rejected offers from Invacare, calling them inadequate. Earlier this month Invacare raised its bid for the third time, to $15 per share.
Shares of Healthdyne surged 1-1/2 to 17 in morning trade.
Invacare could not be reached for comment.
The move by Healthdyne will pressure Invacare to make a decision about the future of its offer, said Matthew Dodds, analyst at Dillon, Read & Co Inc.
"It's tough for Invacare right now, but it's good for Healthdyne shareholders," said Dodds. He thinks Healthdyne may be worth $17 per share.

Wall Street has seen Siemens AG of Germany and Britiann's BOC Group Plc as potential bidders for Healthdyne. But neither company has come forward since Invacare launched its bid in January. Siemens and BOC officials have repeatedly declined comment on Healthdyne.
Invacare has launched a proxy fight to oust Healthdyne's board of directors at the company's July 30 annual meeting.
